In [[mathematics]], an '''induced character''' is the [[character (mathematics)|character]] of the [[group representation|representation]] ''V'' of a [[finite group]] ''G'' [[induced representation|induced]] from a representation ''W'' of a [[subgroup]] ''H'' ≤ ''G''.<!-- Someone should generalize this article. Taku -->  More generally, there is also a notion of the [[induction of a class function|induction]] of a [[class function]] ''f'' on ''H'', <math>\operatorname{Ind}(f)</math>,  given by the formula

:<math>\operatorname{Ind}(f)(s) = \frac{1}{|H|} \sum_{t \in G,\  t^{-1} st \in H} f(t^{-1} st).</math>

If ''f'' is a character of the representation ''W'' of ''H'', then this formula for <math>\operatorname{Ind}(f)</math> calculates the character of the induced representation ''V'' of ''G''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Serre
 | first = Jean-Pierre
 | author-link = Jean-Pierre Serre
 | isbn = 0-387-90190-6
 | location = New York
 | mr = 0450380
 | at = [https://archive.org/details/linearrepresenta1977serr/page/7 7.2, Proposition 20]
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | title = Linear Representations of Finite Groups
 | year = 1977
 | url = https://archive.org/details/linearrepresenta1977serr/page/7
 }}. Translated from the second French edition by Leonard L. Scott.</ref>

The basic result on induced characters is [[Brauer's theorem on induced characters]]. It states that every irreducible character on ''G'' is a [[linear combination]] with integer coefficients of characters induced from [[elementary group|elementary subgroup]]s.
